card.name: Katrilli
card.era: Quadrille forms reached Finland late 18th c.; widespread early/mid-19th c.; Karelian/Skolt forms from Russia late 19th c.
card.tagline: Finland's quadrille - a square or two-line figure set-dance.
card.profile: Katrilli is the Finnish quadrille, a contra/set dance performed in a square (four couples) or two opposing lines, derived from the French cotillion/contredanse and the broader quadrille family (Finnish Wikipedia; Kansantanssin Ystavat). Its turns (vuorot) combine standard figures - circles, vis-a-vis (vastuu), place-changes, pass-throughs (lapikaynti) and karkelo. Two waves reached Finland: a Swedish-derived 'ruotsinkatrilli' across most of the country and a Russian-derived form in Finnish/Russian Karelia and among the Skolt Sami. Steps range from walking and half-run to polka and waltz; Karelian katrillis often feature a male improvisation section (ripaska). Music is led by fiddle, accordion and harmonium.
card.insight: Among Finnish dances recorded by collectors, katrillis are one of the most common types; since the 1980s the improvised 'huutokatrilli' (called/shouted quadrille) has become a late-night highlight at the Kaustinen Folk Music Festival (Finnish Wikipedia; kaustinen.net).
card.image_significance: The Finnish quadrille set dance. A representative image shows folk dress and patterned partner or group figures — Finland.
